head: v0.5.3
title: v0.5.3: gitceps update

steps.title: What this release changes
steps.why: Version 0.5.3 adds gitceps update, makes the installer safe to run again over an existing install, and installs from an archive attached to each release, so GitHub counts installs.
steps.bro: Release day, bro. Gitceps learns to update itself, and the installer can run twice without dropping the bar. Ninety lines. Light weight.

steps.title: gitceps update
steps.why: gitceps update reruns the public installer from main. It refuses when there's no VERSION file, because only install.sh writes one, and tells a Homebrew install to use brew upgrade instead.
steps.bro: One command, fresh install script, straight from main. Installed with Homebrew? Then brew does your reps, not me.

note.text: exec hands the process over to the installer, which replaces this very file while it runs.

steps.title: Safe to run again
steps.why: Before it touches anything, the installer restores a copy an earlier update left behind, refuses a ~/.gitceps that isn't Gitceps, remembers whether he was on, and stops early when this version is already installed.
steps.bro: Look before you lift. Leftover from a cut-off update? Put it back. Somebody else's folder? Hands off. Same version? Rack it and go home.

steps.title: A download GitHub counts
steps.why: The installer now downloads gitceps-<version>.tar.gz attached to the release instead of GitHub's automatic archive, because GitHub only counts downloads of attached files. A workflow builds and attaches that file whenever a release is published.
steps.bro: Every install now counts as a rep. A workflow packs the archive on release, the installer grabs it, and GitHub keeps score.

steps.title: The swap
steps.why: The new copy is built in ~/.gitceps.new and swapped in with two renames, so git never runs hooks from a half-copied folder.
steps.bro: Build it on the side, swap it in two moves. Half-copied hooks folder? Nope. Cut off halfway? The next run puts it back. That's a spotter.

note.text: If an update stops between the two renames, the first check of the next run puts the old copy back.

steps.title: On or off, as before
steps.why: A fresh install turns Gitceps on. An update turns it on again only if it was on, which also points git at the new hooks in case a release moved them. If it was off, it stays off, and the installer says how to turn it on.
steps.bro: Was he on? He's back on. Was he off? He stays off. Updates don't touch your settings, bro.

steps.title: One gap worth knowing
steps.why: Between the two renames, ~/.gitceps doesn't exist. A git command run in that instant finds no hooks, so it runs without the animation and without the secret check.
steps.bro: Two moves means one blink where the gym is empty. A push in that blink skips the secret check. Tiny window. Know it, don't sweat it.

note.text: Worth knowing rather than fixing: the gap lasts two renames.

skipped.reason: Docs: README and CONTRIBUTING describe update and the new release order
The usage line and the header comments now mention update
The check for a folder that isn't Gitceps, moved up to line 15 (step 3)
Workflow setup: the comment on why it exists, its name, permissions, checkout and token, and printing the checksum

summary: Adds gitceps update and makes the installer safe to run again: it restores an interrupted update, refuses folders that aren't Gitceps, skips a version that's already there, swaps the new copy in with two renames, and keeps Gitceps on or off. Installs now download a release archive GitHub counts.
flag: Worth knowing: during the two renames ~/.gitceps briefly doesn't exist, so a git command at that moment runs without hooks (install.sh:50).
